decided_findings.title: The setting that should keep console lines out of reports does not exist in Sentry 11
decided_findings.terms_first: Breadcrumb = a short note Sentry keeps about what happened just before an error — a click, a page change, a line printed to the browser console — and sends with the error report.
decided_findings.scenario: You open a broken alphaTex file. The music engine prints its error to the browser console, and that line can quote text from inside your file. A moment later the player shows E103 and sends a warning to Sentry. The spec promised that this warning leaves the error message out, so nothing from your file goes with it. But the console line goes anyway, as a breadcrumb: the setting the spec uses to stop console breadcrumbs is not an option in Sentry 11. The line does not even compile — and the obvious repair, deleting the unknown option, leaves console breadcrumbs switched on.
decided_findings.whats_wrong: §3.3 passes `console: false` to `breadcrumbsIntegration`. In @sentry/browser 11.0.0 that integration takes only dom, fetch, history, sentry and xhr. Console breadcrumbs now come from a separate default integration named `Console`, and Sentry's 11.0.0 migration guide (MIGRATION.md:1593) says to filter it out. A type-check of the 11.0.0 declarations rejects the line (TS2353). The engine's ScoreLoader prints import failures with console.error at the Info level web/ uses.
evidence_quotes: integrations: [breadcrumbsIntegration({ console: false })],

decided_findings.title: The 'crash-free' health number cannot move in Sentry 11 browsers
decided_findings.terms_first: Release Health = Sentry's count of visits (sessions) per release, each marked healthy, errored, or crashed/unhandled. Decision S4 made its crash-free share the interim health number until NH-52 (CloudWatch burn rates) lands.
decided_findings.scenario: A release goes out with a bug that sends half your visitors to 'Something went wrong'. You open Sentry's Release Health to check the interim health number the spec chose — the crash-free share of visits — and it says 100%. Nothing looks wrong. In Sentry 11 a browser visit is never marked 'crashed', and the reports our error pages send do not count against the number at all.
decided_findings.whats_wrong: In @sentry/browser 11.0.0 a visit hit by an uncaught error is marked 'unhandled', never 'crashed' (client.ts:111-112: 'Unhandled errors don't actually crash the browser, so we report `unhandled` rather than `crashed`'). Sentry's docs: since Sentry 25.9.0 crashes and unhandled errors are counted separately. Every `reportError` call is a handled capture, which only marks the visit 'errored' — and the error pages catch the crash themselves, through `reportError`. So the visits where the page broke never count.
decided_findings.how_to_mark_unhandled: `captureException(error, { mechanism: { handled: false }, captureContext: { tags: { code }, level } })`, or set tags and level with `withScope`. The natural form `captureException(error, { tags: { code }, mechanism: { handled: false } })` fails the type-check and, if forced through, silently stays handled (prepareEvent.ts:347-351).
evidence_quotes: Until NH-52 lands, Sentry Release Health — the crash-free share of visits per release — is the interim front-end health number.
It carries the release, the environment and whether the visit crashed — no file data.
useEffect(() => reportError(error, { code: ERROR.unexpectedCrash }), [error]);

options.cons: A visit where the player engine, the music font or the SoundFont failed (E201–E204) still counts as healthy-but-errored.

+  useEffect(() => reportError(error, { code: ERROR.unexpectedCrash, handled: false }), [error]);

options.label: 2️⃣ Error pages + player failures (E201–E204)
options.what: As 1️⃣, and E201 (engine did not load), E202 (engine error event, e.g. the SoundFont), E203 (font failed) and E204 (font timeout) also send `handled: false`.

options.cons: Failures caused by the visitor's connection (a font download that fails) count too, so the number mixes our bugs with their network.

| Option | Pros | Cons | Best when |

| 1️⃣ Error pages only | only whole-page crashes; pure bug signal | a player that never loads still reads healthy | you want the number to track our code's crashes |

decided_findings.title: Some new end-to-end tests can pass without testing anything, and two cannot pass as written
decided_findings.scenario: Months from now the Sentry build quietly stops sending anything — a renamed variable, a broken route. Every 'sends no error' test still passes: nothing was sent, so nothing bad was found. And case 1 never works at all: a throw inside `page.evaluate` is handed back to the test and never reaches the page's error handler, so 'sends an error' fails on day one.
decided_findings.whats_wrong: Cases 3, 4 and 5 only check that something is absent, so they pass when the recorder captured nothing — the trap page-errors.ts already records from NH-291 (page-errors.ts:112-117). Case 5's 'nothing is sent' cannot pass literally: S4 sends a session ping on every visit. Case 4 must wait for NH-335, which fires only after the score is drawn. Spike (Chromium 149): a direct throw in `page.evaluate` reaches neither window.onerror nor Playwright's pageerror; a throw scheduled with setTimeout reaches both.
